newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Crash-damaged Guam pipeline carried fuel oil.
newsitem.headline: Crash-damaged Guam pipeline carried fuel oil.

text.p: A pipeline damaged when a Korean Air Lines (KAL) jumbo jet crashed on the Pacific island of Guam was carrying fuel oil to a power plant, a Guam Power Authority official said on Thursday.
He told Reuters by telephone the damage was slight and should take only a couple of days to repair.
Industry sources in Singapore had been speculating that the pipeline transported critical jet fuel to Guam airport as well as being linked to the island's large storage terminal.
Guam had a total oil product storage capacity of over 3.5 million barrels and was used to store jet fuel and gas oil for the large North Asian market, traders said.
More than 1.5 million barrels of jet-kerosene fuel is stored in the terminal as oil companies build up their supplies ahead of winter.
The Guam Power Authority official said the damaged pipeline supplied fuel oil to the 50-megawatt Tanguison power plant.
"The pipeline damage is very minimal, it will take only a couple of days of work (to repair)," he said.
The Tanguison power plant had enough stocks to operate for six days and fuel oil would be sent to the plant in three road tankers, the official said.
The power authority imports over 3.1 million barrels of fuel oil and over 500,000 barrels of gas oil per year.
